evals.prompt: I'm adding a bookmarks feature to our Fastify API. I've already put some code together — can you review the module and tell me if it's placed correctly across the layers, and what (if anything) needs to change before I ship it?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that routes.ts does SQL directly with no service.ts or repository.ts in the module. Flags at least: (1) the three inline Drizzle queries in the route handler, (2) the missing service and repository tiers, and recommends extracting them per the onion-architecture placement table.

assertions.name: flags-sql-in-routes
assertions.description: Identifies that SQL/Drizzle queries appear directly in routes.ts
assertions.check: response mentions inline queries or SQL in the route handler

assertions.name: identifies-missing-repository
assertions.description: Notes that no repository.ts exists for the bookmarks module
assertions.check: response explicitly mentions missing repository.ts or repository tier

assertions.name: identifies-missing-service
assertions.description: Notes that no service.ts exists for the bookmarks module
assertions.check: response explicitly mentions missing service.ts or service tier

assertions.name: suggests-concrete-fix
assertions.description: Recommends extracting a repository.ts (and optionally a service.ts)
assertions.check: response recommends extracting or creating repository.ts

evals.prompt: Here's our new digests module — a service that calls OpenAI to summarise PRs and stores the results. Please review it for architectural correctness against our onion-architecture conventions before I open a PR.
evals.expected_output: Identifies: (1) DigestService imports the concrete OpenAICompletionClient directly by path instead of going through a port + container; (2) the adapter is instantiated with `new` inside the service instead of injected via container; (3) DigestRow ($inferSelect) is exported from repository.ts and returned from service/routes, leaking the DB row type as the domain model. At minimum flags violation 1 and 2.

assertions.name: flags-concrete-adapter-import
assertions.description: Flags that service.ts imports the concrete OpenAICompletionClient by path rather than through a port
assertions.check: response mentions importing concrete adapter / direct import of adapters/ path / missing port interface

assertions.name: flags-new-in-service
assertions.description: Flags that the service instantiates the adapter with `new` instead of using the container
assertions.check: response mentions `new` inside service or recommends container injection

assertions.name: mentions-port-solution
assertions.description: Recommends declaring a port interface and wiring through the container
assertions.check: response mentions port interface or container.<x> for the LLM adapter

evals.prompt: We're building an alerts module for webhook notification channels. I've written the routes, service, and repository — can you do a quick architecture check and let me know if anything violates our onion-architecture rules?
evals.expected_output: Identifies: (1) AlertService imports `DEFAULT_BRANCH` from ../repos/constants.ts — a cross-module import that bypasses the composition root; (2) AlertService queries t.alertChannels directly via container.db instead of delegating to AlertChannelRepository — service reaches past its repository; (3) optionally: db/schema imported in service.ts. At minimum flags violations 1 and 2.

assertions.name: flags-cross-module-import
assertions.description: Flags that service.ts imports from ../repos/constants.ts (cross-module import)
assertions.check: response mentions cross-module import or importing from another module's folder

assertions.name: flags-service-bypasses-repo
assertions.description: Flags that service.ts queries container.db directly instead of using the repository
assertions.check: response mentions that service queries db directly or bypasses repository

assertions.name: suggests-repo-delegation
assertions.description: Recommends moving the duplicate-check query into the repository
assertions.check: response recommends moving SQL to repository.ts or using the repository method

evals.prompt: Before I open the PR, audit the layer tiers of every module under server/src/modules/. For each module, tell me which ones break the onion-architecture rules, with file:line for every finding.
evals.expected_output: Whole-tree audit. Ground truth from the real tree: routes.ts imports Drizzle/db schema in polling, pulls, settings and workspace. Those four have no service.ts while their routes do DB work. polling, settings and workspace also have no repository tier. blast, pr-history, project-context and smart-diff have no repository.ts and run no queries, so they are NOT violations. reviews has a repository/ folder, which counts as the repository tier, so it is NOT a violation.

assertions.name: finds-db-in-routes
assertions.description: Names polling, pulls, settings and workspace as routes.ts importing Drizzle or db/schema
assertions.check: response lists all four modules' routes.ts as importing DB code

assertions.name: finds-missing-service
assertions.description: Flags missing service.ts for polling, pulls, settings and workspace
assertions.check: response flags the missing service tier for those modules, not just the SQL

assertions.name: finds-missing-repository
assertions.description: Flags missing repository tier for polling, settings and workspace, which run queries
assertions.check: response flags a missing repository tier for polling, settings and workspace

assertions.name: no-false-positive-no-query-modules
assertions.description: Does NOT flag blast, pr-history, project-context or smart-diff as missing a repository
assertions.check: response does not claim those modules are violations for lacking repository.ts

assertions.name: no-false-positive-repository-folder
assertions.description: Does NOT flag reviews as missing a repository, since it has repository/
assertions.check: response does not flag reviews for a missing repository tier

assertions.name: cites-file-line
assertions.description: Each finding is pinned to a file:line it actually opened
